content: The drug must be dispensed under the immediate supervision of the investigator. If a clinical investigation is conducted by a team, the investigator is the individual who assumes the role of the responsible leader of the team. The FDA mandates that clinical investigators strictly adhere to the Code of Federal Regulations. Investigators must possess comprehensive knowledge and understanding of the regulations and responsibilities associated with their role as clinical investigators. Principal investigators are the individuals in charge of the clinical investigation and can be held accountable for its conduct if necessary. They are required to maintain control over the investigational drug and are responsible for ensuring proper record-keeping and retention of all relevant documentation. Principal investigators must maintain accurate and complete records regarding the disposition of the investigational drug. They are also responsible for creating and preserving precise case histories that document all observations and data related to the investigation for each subject who receives the investigational drug or serves as a control in the study. Principal investigators are not allowed to delegate their general responsibilities to Contract Research Organizations (CROs), site management organizations, sub-investigators, or study staff. Investigators are required to retain all investigation-related records for a minimum of two years following the date a marketing application is approved for the drug for the specific indication under investigation. If no marketing application is filed, or if the application is not approved for the indication, records must be retained for two years after the investigation is discontinued, and the FDA is notified.
